title: Selftest scenario asserting LICENSE classifies as metadata
objective: Add a scripts/selftest scenario pinning that the root LICENSE path classifies as metadata, so a future edit that drops LICENSE from candidate-fingerprint's METADATA_FILES fails the tooling suite instead of silently reclassifying the license as product content.
specReferences: the frozen design's candidate-fingerprint classification rules (product/metadata/unknown, fail-closed)
acceptance: a scripts/selftest scenario asserts that the root path LICENSE classifies as metadata
the scenario fails if LICENSE is removed from candidate-fingerprint's METADATA_FILES, and fails if LICENSE is reclassified as product content
./scripts/selftest reports one additional scenario and still exits 0 with 0 failed
nonGoals: no change to scripts/candidate-fingerprint (LICENSE was already added to METADATA_FILES when FJ-051 was opened)
no change to LICENSE or to any other product file
no weakening of any existing selftest assertion
nextAction: add the metadata-classification scenario to scripts/selftest and prove it fails when LICENSE is dropped from METADATA_FILES
notes: Opened 2026-10-03 by PM as the audited split of FJ-051 acceptance criterion 4: 'a selftest scenario asserting LICENSE classifies as metadata lands once the in-flight selftest reformat is merged'. That reformat (FJ-061) has since merged, so the criterion became actionable, but the scenario lives in scripts/selftest while FJ-051's allowedFiles is exactly [LICENSE]. Per the owner's standing preference (2026-09-30) the unmet criterion was split into this dedicated ticket with an audit trail rather than widening FJ-051's allowedFiles.
FJ-051 met criteria 1, 2, 3 and 5; criterion 4 is owned here.

Coverage context: scripts/selftest already exercises candidate-fingerprint determinism, evidence-dir exclusion, canonical-form recomputation, tracked-dirty content and task-fingerprint classification for .agent/work and docs paths, but no scenario pins the classification of a root-level METADATA_FILES entry such as LICENSE, README.md or Dockerfile. Without this scenario, deleting LICENSE from METADATA_FILES would make the license classify as product content, which would change candidate fingerprints for every future candidate and stale stage artifacts, with nothing in the suite objecting.

Candidate-fingerprint already classifies LICENSE as metadata: METADATA_FILES gained LICENSE when FJ-051 was opened, and 'candidate-fingerprint task .agent/work/FJ-051/state.json' reports class metadata with requiredStages specifier,coder,cleaner,qa derived from that class.

Measured behaviour to preserve: unlike .agent/** evidence, adding or changing LICENSE DOES change the candidate fingerprint (80852a3b20015001679e3171fe0271619845cf02203b70f2cb59470b976af21c before FJ-051's LICENSE, 8c80ab298a252de531dbf9f61a0f67e866fdf5e091cbf8fb80d272d988305c29 after). The metadata class governs task fingerprints and stage policy, not candidate hashing, so a scenario must not assert that LICENSE is excluded from the candidate fingerprint.
Test 75 of 75 scenarios currently pass; this ticket is expected to make it 76.
